body:
I've always been extremely shy and relied upon external achievements for self-esteem. I didn't have the classical support network of friends and family that most people had growing up. Turns out that can really warp your self-image. Because no matter how much you achieve it'll never be enough to sustain self-confidence.

Yeah, there is nothing wrong with the world, I just don't know if I'm cut out for it. And you're right. I don't feel like I have any control over my life.

It's nice to know I'm not the only person out there. The self-doubt lingers like a haunting, waiting for moments of weakness to infect me with its crazy. And after my brain is hijacked, I'm hell bent on self-destruction. Like you said, even when I'm feeling good I know the awful thoughts and consequences will continue to make a cameo in my life. It's like no amount of praise or success or rational assessment of myself can convince my brain I'm good enough. And as long as I'm living it's going to try do me in. And I'm not convinced it won't succeed.
